title: Harmonize adaptive-retries, auth bridge, and generator stream ergonomics across Python/TS/Go
author: Samira Gomez
description: Motivation: Teams using Redwood SDKs reported subtle differences in retry semantics, credential handoff, and generator/async-stream ergonomics across python/typescript/go. This caused production surprises (double-retries, token thrash, and inconsistent streaming iterators). Goal: provide a compact, opinionated cross-SDK surface that (1) standardizes adaptive retry profiles, (2) introduces a lightweight auth-bridge interface for delegated refresh/fanout, and (3) smooths generator/pullstream ergonomics so examples and docs match behavior across languages. Summary of changes: added an SDK-agnostic adaptive retry table + presets, implemented an auth-bridge shim in internal/auth that SDKs can opt into, refactored generator iterator helpers in sdks/python, sdks/typescript, and sdks/go to expose a consistent pull()/close() shape, and updated tests + examples. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve current behavior for consumers that do not opt into the new retry presets or auth-bridge. Migration notes are contained in release_notes. Checklist: - [x] design doc and API sketches attached in the PR thread - [x] python/typescript/go implementations wired to shared retry presets - [x] integration tests for auth handoff + token refresh under flakey network - [x] docs / examples updated - [x] changelog and release note drafted Related work: ENG-1987 (retry matrix), ENG-2004 (stream ergonomics), SUP-4321 (customer incident: double-refresh during high-concurrency).
